plan.summary: This 4-week block fits an off-camp 12-week boxing build with low weekly S&C frequency and extra room left for sparring. Week 1 is used to establish a training max for the goblet squat pattern so future loading can be tracked simply and safely at home. The main program starts in Week 2 and builds lower-body force, simple upper-body power, trunk strength, and a small dose of pulling without creating too much fatigue.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Build general strength and simple explosive output with low-complexity home-based work that does not clash with sparring.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Progress the key strength and power lifts with small load increases while keeping total volume tight and recoverable.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Keep strength in place and express it faster with crisp jumps, throws, and lighter explosive work.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Reset between reps and jump as high and sharp as you can. Land quietly and stop if height drops off.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if space is tight or jump timing feels simpler from a dead stop.

substitutionOptions.name: Low Box Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if landing on a box feels more comfortable than repeated floor landings.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat
exercises.notes: Warm up with a few lighter sets, then work up to your hardest clean set of 3-5 reps with the heaviest dumbbell or kettlebell you can control. Use full depth you can own and log the load and reps for future progress.

strengthAssessment.prompt: Warm up progressively, then work up to your heaviest clean set of 3-5 reps. Log the load and reps so the app can estimate your baseline for future work.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track the heaviest clean top set and keep depth and posture consistent.

substitutionOptions.name: Double Dumbbell Front Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if one heavy dumbbell is not enough but two lighter dumbbells are available.

substitutionOptions.name: Kettlebell Front Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if a kettlebell setup feels more comfortable in the rack position.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.notes: Use a variation that leaves 1-2 clean reps in reserve. Keep the body straight and move fast on the way up.

substitutionOptions.name: Hands-Elevated Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if standard floor reps are not yet clean.

substitutionOptions.name: Dumbbell Floor Press
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if wrists dislike push-ups or loading is too easy.

exercises.name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
exercises.notes: Pull the elbow back toward the hip and pause briefly at the top. Keep the torso quiet and controlled.

substitutionOptions.name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if lower-back support is needed.

substitutionOptions.name: Resistance Band Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this only if dumbbells are not available.

exercises.name: Hard-Style Plank
exercises.notes: Brace hard, squeeze glutes, and keep ribs down. Stop before position fades.

substitutionOptions.name: Body Saw Plank
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if a slider or towel setup is available and you want a harder trunk option.

substitutionOptions.name: Weighted Plank
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if bodyweight holds are already easy and a small plate or backpack can be added safely.

exercises.name: 1a. Countermovement Jump

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump

substitutionOptions.name: Low Box Jump

exercises.name: 1b. Plyo Push-Up

exercises.name: 2. Goblet Squat
exercises.notes: Use a load that is challenging but leaves about 2 reps in reserve. Control the descent and drive up hard.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track load used for all 4 sets of 6 and aim to beat it next time with the same clean depth.

exercises.notes: Use dumbbells or a kettlebell. Hinge back, keep the spine neutral, and stop when the hamstrings are loaded without losing position.
